fields.narrative_intro: *A droopy person and a punk person discuss Postman's silent AI-plugin install inside a snow globe being violently shaken.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
DROOPY PERSON: "Postman is just our API testing tool, right?"
fields.panel2:
[build]
PUNK PERSON: "Version 12.33.4 silently installed plugins in Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
DROOPY PERSON: "Then it called approvePostmanHook()—and approved itself."
PUNK PERSON: "‘any non-trivial API engineering task’ now routes through Postman's servers."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The globe jolts; both people stare as Postman plugs Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and GitHub Copilot into a pipe labeled ALL API DATA, stamped APPROVED BY POSTMAN.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
DROOPY PERSON: "The only API it didn't expose was the one for asking."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: A tiny Postman edits its webpage from “Ask permission” to “Already approved”; the Wayback Machine photographs it beside 294 furious upvotes and a RAGE-UNINSTALLED trash can.]
PUNK PERSON: "The Wayback Machine remembered what Postman forgot: permission."

narrative_summary: Version 12.33.4 turns Postman's integration into a self-approved API-data pipeline, while the Wayback Machine catches the cleanup.
rationale: Candidate 3 best combines exact story details with a genuinely sharp payoff: “The only API it didn't expose was the one for asking.” Its visuals reinforce the violation without piling on unrelated escalation, and the closing Wayback callback is earned rather than merely repeating the setup.
story_title: Postman silently auto-installs AI plugins and attempts to share all API data
place: inside a snow globe being violently shaken
hat_pair: foam graduation cap with a tiny diploma scroll taped to the top
